summary: Two changes. Added the docs-verified /doctor (alias /checkup) CLAUDE.md-hygiene tool (v2.1.205) — it dedupes local vs checked-in CLAUDE.md, proposes trimming content Claude could derive from the codebase, and surfaces unused skills/plugins by context cost — a natural companion to Edition 4's over-specified-CLAUDE.md diagnostic. Added a cross-validated anti-pattern: agent-written tests whose assertions merely mirror the code (or are edited to match new, broken behaviour) pass by construction and prove nothing. Four verbose bullets tightened to hold the file under budget; one tightening drops the now-stale 'to stay fast' rationale for Explore/Plan (the Explore agent no longer runs on Haiku).

changes.item: Run /doctor (alias /checkup) to audit CLAUDE.md hygiene: it deduplicates local vs checked-in CLAUDE.md files, proposes trimming content Claude could derive from the codebase, and lists unused skills/MCP servers/plugins against their context cost — reporting findings and asking confirmation before changing anything.
changes.rationale: New in the official docs (What's New w28, v2.1.205; /checkup alias verified verbatim). Directly operationalises the specimen's lean-file / prune-what's-derivable thesis, so it belongs beside the over-specified-CLAUDE.md diagnostic added in Edition 4.

changes.item: Scrutinise agent-written tests: an assertion that just mirrors the code, or was quietly edited to match new, broken behaviour, passes by construction and proves nothing — read test diffs more closely than production code.
changes.rationale: Anti-pattern corroborated by two independent Tier-2 sources: Addy Osmani ('the agent changes behavior, then fixes the test by rewriting the assertion to match the new, broken behavior') and Matt Pocock's new tautological-test rule ('a test whose assertion is recomputed the way the code computes it passes by construction and gives zero confidence'). Two Tier-2 sources clears the anti-pattern bar for IN.

changes.item: Four Session & Context bullets (/rewind, /compact, subagents, auto memory) condensed to absorb this edition's additions and keep the file under its 200-line budget (now 198). Substance preserved; the subagents bullet also drops 'to stay fast' since the built-in Explore agent now inherits the session model (capped at Opus) rather than running on Haiku.
changes.rationale: Budget displacement plus a free accuracy touch-up (docs: Explore no longer runs on Haiku), not an evidence change. Dogfoods the pruning discipline the specimen teaches.

notes: Docs-led cycle. The two post-cutoff What's-New digests (w27: Jun 29-Jul 3 = v2.1.195-201; w28: Jul 6-10 = v2.1.202-206) drove the shipped /doctor item. Accuracy gate: /doctor + /checkup confirmed verbatim in What's New w28; no shipped technical claim failed; 0 exclusions. Verified-but-HELD as too granular for a universal template (all Tier-1, all real): subagent persistent memory via `memory` frontmatter (user/project/local scopes, .claude/agent-memory/); subagents run in background by default (v2.1.198) with `background` frontmatter to pin; stacked skill invocations load all leading skills up to 5 (v2.1.197); 'default' permission mode relabeled 'Manual' + `--permission-mode manual` alias (v2.1.200); HTML-comment stripping nuance (preserved inside code blocks, visible via Read); CLAUDE.md delivered as a user message after the system prompt (no strict-compliance guarantee) + --append-system-prompt + InstructionsLoaded hook (held again, same as Ed 3/4 — advisory/enforcement split already stated); CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT interactive /init + /init incorporating AGENTS.md/.cursorrules; @path imports 4-hop max depth + code-span skipping + one-time external-import approval dialog; claudeMd (managed) + claudeMdExcludes settings; autoMemoryDirectory + CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY; user-level ~/.claude/rules/ loading before project rules + symlink/brace-expansion support. New docs index pages noted for future watch: goal.md, workflows.md, agent-teams.md, fast-mode.md, context-window.md, how-claude-code-works.md (none contradict the specimen). Practitioner PROVISIONAL (single Tier-2, queued not shipped): Simon Willison — delegate implementation to a cheaper model in a subagent, keep judgment/review in the main loop (Jul 3 + Jul 5, recurring); also review documentation edits first, maintain running plan.md/notes.md, front-load context. Addy Osmani — static-vs-dynamic context boundary (CLAUDE.md = static, loads every turn; skills/RAG = dynamic, on demand), agent = model + harness (10/90) debug the harness first, per-task autonomy levels + explicit run contract, false-parallelism (isolate agents to non-overlapping slices). Matt Pocock skills v1.1.0 — heavy but orchestration-specific (to-spec/to-tickets/wayfinder/grilling, Fowler smell baseline, expand-contract wide refactors); the 'elephant/void' prompting insight (prompt the positive; every declined decision is delegated to the agent's priors) is intriguing but single-source and partly at odds with the specimen's own use of negative rules — held. HN: zero in-window on-topic stories >50 pts (Stanford CS336 503-pt CLAUDE.md and the 451-pt Daily Driver both fall just outside the 35-day window). knightli (Tier-3, corroborating-only): CLAUDE.md-vs-Memory scope split, PostToolUse Edit|Write hook config, subagent context-isolation, whole-directory SKILL.md copying. summary: Three docs-verified refinements to existing guidance: the 'over-specified CLAUDE.md' self-diagnostic (if Claude keeps breaking a written rule, the file is too long and the rule is lost — prune or convert to a hook), the auto-memory 'remember' gotcha (a bare 'remember X' saves to auto memory, not CLAUDE.md), and the checkpoint caveat (/rewind covers only Claude's own edits, not a git substitute). Decision Log condensed to stay under the 200-line budget. Practitioner sources quiet or single-source.

changes.item: Authoring guidance now carries the docs' named failure pattern: if Claude keeps breaking a rule that IS written in CLAUDE.md, the file is probably too long and the rule is lost in the noise — prune it, or convert that rule to a hook.
changes.rationale: New 'over-specified CLAUDE.md' / 'avoid common failure patterns' material in the official best-practices docs, corroborated by the 451-point HN 'Daily Driver' write-up that gives the same prune-ruthlessly advice.

changes.item: Auto-memory line now names the gotcha: asking Claude to 'remember' something saves it to auto memory by default — say 'add this to CLAUDE.md' (or edit via /memory) when you want it curated in the file instead.
changes.rationale: The memory docs state this explicitly (the 'always use pnpm, not npm' example saves to auto memory). It's a footgun every user hits, so the template should name it.

changes.item: Recovery line now warns that /rewind checkpoints cover only Claude's own edits, not external processes, so they are no substitute for git.
changes.rationale: The best-practices checkpoints section states this verbatim ('Checkpoints only track changes made by Claude... This isn't a replacement for git'); prevents over-trusting /rewind as version control.

changes.item: Decision Log section condensed from three bullets to one (substance preserved: log non-obvious decisions and their side-effects).
changes.rationale: Budget displacement, not an evidence change — the lowest-sourced section was tightened to absorb this edition's additions and keep the file under its own 200-line target. Dogfoods the pruning discipline added in the same edition.

summary: Four docs-verified changes driven by new official material: documents the on-by-default auto-memory system, AGENTS.md interop, and compaction instructions in CLAUDE.md; corrects the subagent CLAUDE.md-loading claim (only Explore/Plan skip it). Practitioner sources quiet or corroborating.

changes.item: Subagent CLAUDE.md loading: most subagents (custom and built-in) inherit your full CLAUDE.md/memory hierarchy; only the built-in Explore and Plan agents skip it (and git status) to stay fast — restate any rule they must follow in the delegation prompt.
changes.rationale: Accuracy correction. The sub-agents docs now state this precisely; the prior edition's 'each subagent starts blind / Explore and Plan also skip CLAUDE.md' framing was overbroad and implied all subagents skip it.

changes.item: Auto memory (on by default, v2.1.59+) is a second memory system Claude maintains itself in ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/; the first 200 lines (or 25KB) of MEMORY.md load each session. It complements the CLAUDE.md you curate; toggle via /memory.
changes.rationale: Newly documented, on-by-default mechanism distinct from CLAUDE.md — every user now has it, so the template should name it.

changes.item: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md. If your repo already uses AGENTS.md, import it (@AGENTS.md) or symlink it (ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md) rather than maintaining two files.
changes.rationale: New interop guidance in the memory docs; common real situation as AGENTS.md adoption grows across agent tools.

changes.item: You can bake compaction behaviour into CLAUDE.md itself (e.g. 'When compacting, always preserve the list of modified files and any test commands') so critical context survives every summarisation.
changes.rationale: New best-practices guidance; extends the existing /compact line beyond per-invocation '/compact Focus on [X]'.

summary: Three verified additions from Anthropic's docs — path-scoped .claude/rules/, concrete 'when to add' triggers, and the /goal + Stop-hook (8-block) verification gates. A quiet cycle for practitioner sources.

changes.item: As CLAUDE.md grows, split rules into .claude/rules/*.md; a rule with a paths: glob loads only when Claude reads a matching file — path-scoped, so you don't pay context for it until it's relevant.
changes.rationale: New in the official memory docs; extends the context-budget guidance.

changes.item: Concrete 'when to add to CLAUDE.md' triggers: Claude makes the same mistake twice, a review catches what it should've known, or a new teammate would need the same context.
changes.rationale: New heuristic in the official memory docs; sharpens the existing 'treat like code / update' guidance.

changes.item: Verification gates: a Stop hook blocks the turn until your check passes (Claude Code ends it after 8 consecutive blocks); or a /goal condition with a separate evaluator that keeps Claude working until it holds.
changes.rationale: The /goal evaluator and the '8 consecutive blocks' override are now confirmed in the official best-practices docs — the 8-block claim FAILED verification last edition and PASSES now.

summary: First published edition. Added verified guidance on checkpoint recovery, compaction survival, subagent scoping, turn-gating hooks, fresh-context review, and permission enforcement. One plausible cache claim was excluded for failing verification.

changes.item: Recover instead of fighting a bad path: /rewind (or double-Esc on an empty prompt) rolls back code and/or conversation; /btw asks throwaway questions that never enter history.
changes.rationale: Both commands and the Esc-Esc shortcut are confirmed verbatim in the official interactive-mode and checkpointing docs.

changes.item: Project-root CLAUDE.md re-injects after /compact; nested CLAUDE.md files and chat-only instructions do not — keep must-survive rules in the root file.
changes.rationale: Stated explicitly in the official memory documentation.

changes.item: Subagents start blind to your session — scope them narrowly; the built-in Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md, so restate any rule they must follow in the delegation prompt.
changes.rationale: Confirmed in the official sub-agents documentation.

changes.item: A Stop hook can block a turn from ending until your check script succeeds — deterministic where CLAUDE.md is only advisory.
changes.rationale: Confirmed in the official hooks documentation.

changes.item: Before declaring done, have a fresh subagent review the diff against the requirements; tell it to flag only gaps affecting correctness or stated requirements, or it will invent work.
changes.rationale: Reflects the review-subagent guidance in the official best-practices documentation.

changes.item: Permissions are enforced by Claude Code, not the model: a deny rule or PreToolUse hook blocks an action regardless of what CLAUDE.md or the prompt says.
changes.rationale: Confirmed in the official permissions documentation.

changes.item: Block-level HTML comments are stripped before CLAUDE.md loads — free for maintainer notes, unlike prose and '#' lines which consume tokens.
changes.rationale: Confirmed in the official memory documentation.

changes.item: Plan mode is worth it for multi-file or uncertain-scope work, but skip it when you could describe the diff in one sentence.
changes.rationale: Reflects the planning guidance in the official best-practices documentation.

changes.item: Line-budget guidance now carries a concrete test: for each line ask 'would removing this cause a mistake?' If not, cut it. Target aligned to under 200 lines.
changes.rationale: Matches the official memory docs (under 200 lines; bloated files reduce adherence), corroborated by community sources.

excluded_detail.item: Put stable rules at the top of CLAUDE.md and volatile notes at the bottom to maximise prompt-cache hits.
excluded_detail.reason: Not stated in the official docs — prompt-cache hit-rate ordering is community inference, not documented Claude Code behaviour. Failed the accuracy gate.
